'''Adreian Payne''' (born February 19, 1991) is an American [[college basketball]] player for [[Michigan State Spartans men's basketball|Michigan State]] where he is a senior on the [[2013–14 Michigan State Spartans men's basketball team|2013–14 team]].

==High school career==
Payne played high school basketball for [[Jefferson Township High School (Dayton, Ohio)|Jefferson High School]]. He posted averages of 15.6 points, 11.3 rebounds and 4.0 blocks as a senior. As a senior, he led Jefferson to a Division IV state championship and a 19-5 record. The ''[[Dayton Daily News]]'' named him first team All-Area.<ref name=Msu />

==College career==
[[File:US_Navy_111110-N-DR144-711_Michigan_State_University_basketball_player_Adreian_Payne_dunks_during_a_practice_in_the_basketball_arena_on_the_flight.jpg|thumb|left|Adreian Payne practicing before the 2011 [[Carrier Classic]]]]
As a freshman, Payne averaged 2.5 points and 2.4 rebounds per game, playing in 34 games.<ref name=Msu>{{cite web|title=5 Adreian Payne|url=http://www.msuspartans.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/adreian_payne_725881.html|work=[[Michigan State Spartans]]|publisher=[[Michigan State University]]|accessdate=February 27, 2014}}</ref>

In his sophomore season, he led the team in blocks (39) and finished seventh in the Big 10. In 37 games (36 starts), he averaged 7.0 points and 4.2 rebounds per game. He was an Academic All-Big Ten selection.<ref name=Msu />

As a junior, Payne led the Big Ten in free-throw percentage (.848) and blocked a total of 46 shots, good for sixth all-time for a Michigan State player. In 36 games (324 starts), he averaged 10.5 points and 7.6 rebounds in 25.6 minutes per game.<ref name=Msu /> Payne was named to the Second Team All Big Ten, along with Michigan State teammates [[Keith Appling]] and [[Gary Harris]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://grfx.cstv.com/photos/schools/big10/sports/m-baskbl/auto_pdf/2012-13/misc_non_event/2013AllBigTen.pdf|title=2012-13 All-Big Ten Men’s Basketball Team|accessdate=February 27, 2014|date=March 11, 2013|publisher=[[CBS Interactive]]|work=BigTen.org}}</ref>

Coming into his senior year, Payne was on the preseason [[Naismith College Player of the Year|Naismith]] and [[John R. Wooden Award|Wooden]] Award watchlists.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.bigten.org/blog/2013/11/wooden-award-preseason-top-50-includes-ten-big-ten-players.html|title=
Wooden Award Preseason Top 50 Includes Ten Big Ten Players|date=November 12, 2013|accessdate=February 27, 2014|publisher=[[CBS Interactive]]|work=BigTen.org}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.bigten.org/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/112213aaa.html|title=Big Ten Men's Basketball Release - Weekend Edition: Big Ten went 11-1 during the week |date=November 21, 2013|accessdate=February 27, 2013|publisher=[[CBS Interactive]]|work=BigTen.org}}</ref> [[CBS Sports]] selected him to the preseason Third Team All-America.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.cbssports.com/collegebasketball/eye-on-college-basketball/23858735/cbssportscom-201314-preseason-allamerican-teams|title=CBSSports.com 2013-14 Preseason All-American teams|accessdate=October 12, 2013|date=February 27, 2013|publisher=[[CBS Sports]]}}</ref> He was named to the Midseason Wooden Award Top 25 watchlist.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.bigten.org/blog/2014/01/four-big-ten-players-named-to-wooden-award-midseason-top-25-list.html|title=Four Big Ten Players Named to Wooden Award Midseason Top 25 List|accessdate=February 27, 2013|date=January 22, 2014|publisher=[[CBS Interactive]]|work=BigTen.org}}</ref> Payne was twice named Big Ten Player of the Week.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.bigten.org/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/111813aaa.html|title=Michigan State and Indiana Earn Weekly Men's Basketball Honors: Michigan State's Adreian Payne named Player of the Week; Indiana's Noah Vonleh tabbed Freshman of the Week |accessdate=2013-11-19|date=2013-11-18|publisher=[[CBS Interactive]]|work=BigTen.org}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.bigten.org/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/122313aaa.html|title=Michigan State, Indiana and Michigan Earn Weekly Men's Basketball Honors|accessdate=2013-12-24|date=2013-12-23|publisher=[[CBS Interactive]]|work=BigTen.org}}</ref> He missed 
seven games due to suffering an ankle injury.<ref>{{cite news|title=Adreian Payne expected to play Thursday against Penn State|url=http://www.lansingstatejournal.com/article/20140204/GW0201/302040021/Adreian-Payne-expected-play-Thursday-against-Penn-State|accessdate=February 28, 2014|newspaper=[[Lansing State Journal]]|date=February 4, 2014}}</ref> At the conclusion of the regular season Payne was named Second Team All-Big Ten.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.bigten.org/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/031014aag.html|title=Big Ten Announces 2014 Men's Basketball Postseason Honors: Michigan's Stauskas named Big Ten Player of the Year|accessdate=2014-03-10|date=2014-03-10|publisher=[[CBS Interactive]]|work=BigTen.org}}</ref>

==Friendship with Lacey Holsworth==
During the 2013-2014 college basketball season, Payne's friendship with Lacey Holsworth, an 8-year-old cancer patient, gained national media attention.<ref>{{cite web|title=This Pair's Beautiful Friendship Will Fill Your Heart with March Gladness|url=http://www.huffingtonpost.com/2014/03/24/adreian-payne-lacey-friendship-michigan-state_n_5021300.html|publisher=Huffington Post|accessdate=9 April 2014}}</ref> Their friendship started when Payne met Holsworth during a team-sponsored hospital visit in 2011 and the two began to text and talk frequently afterward.<ref>{{cite web|title=Adreian Payne Forms a Special Bond with Girl Battling Cancer|url=http://www.people.com/people/article/0,,20800862,00.html|publisher=People.com|accessdate=9 April 2014}}</ref> Holsworth, who battled with a nerve cancer known as [[neuroblastoma]], accompanied Payne at center court on Senior Night and helped him cut down the nets after [[2013-14 Michigan State Spartans men's basketball team]] won the [[Big Ten Men's Basketball Tournament]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Biggest Star of March Madness Is an 8-Year-Old Girl Fighting Cancer|url=http://mashable.com/2014/03/27/march-madness-lacey-michigan-state/|publisher=Mashable.com|accessdate=9 April 2014}}</ref> Holsworth, also known as "Princess Lacey", died from her cancer on April 8, 2014.<ref>{{cite web|title=Lacey Holsworth, 8, dies of cancer|url=http://espn.go.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/10754327/michigan-state-spartans-adreian-payne-mourning-loss-princess-lacey-cancer|publisher=ESPN.com|accessdate=9 April 2014}}</ref>
